recap.back_html: The question at the top, split into sub-questions until each leaf is answerable with one piece of analysis.
Mutually exclusive: no item in two branches. Collectively exhaustive: the branches cover everything.
A hypothesis and the analysis that would prove or disprove it.
Those likely to explain most, which you can test quickly. Drop branches that would not change the decision.

lessons.takeaway_html: Turn a vague question into a tree of sub-questions. Make each split mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive, give each branch a hypothesis and a test, and drop branches that would not change the decision.
lessons.title: Break a vague question into an issue tree

recap.back_html: The answer first, then three or four MECE points that answer why or how, then the evidence under each.
What the reader accepts, what changed, the question it raises. Then the answer.
Full-sentence takeaways, such as "First-year leavers are flat since March". Never "Findings".
Read only the first sentence of each paragraph. The argument should still hold.

lessons.takeaway_html: Put the answer first, then three or four MECE points that support it, then the evidence. Open with situation, complication and question, and write headings as takeaways.
lessons.title: Lead with the answer, write in a pyramid

recap.back_html: Remote chance 0 to 5%, highly unlikely 10 to 20%, unlikely 25 to 35%, realistic possibility 40 to under 50%, likely 55 to 75%, highly likely 80 to 90%, almost certain 95 to under 100%.
To avoid false precision. A value in a gap, such as 50%, forces you to decide which way the evidence leans.
Probability: how likely the event is. Confidence: how good the evidence is. Report both, separately.
The judgement first, as a range, then the one limitation that matters and what would change your mind.

lessons.takeaway_html: Use fixed probability words with ranges behind them, keep confidence in the evidence separate, give ranges rather than points, and lead with the judgement before the one limitation that matters.
lessons.title: Explain uncertainty to leaders

summary: Issue trees, answer-first writing in a pyramid, and explaining uncertainty to leaders.
title: Structure your thinking and writing
